Q: Is there a standard definition for __cplusplus in c++14? A:

cppreference has information on the standard values of the __cplusplus macro in the section "Predefined macros." Currently the standard values are:

199711L (C++98 or C++03)
201103L (C++11)
201402L (C++14)
201703L (C++17)
202002L (C++20)
202302L (C++23)
202603L (C++26)

The macro's value for any given version isn't firmly established until the final standard is published. Therefore, as of June 2019, there was no way to know what the macro value for C++2a would be (and as of Feb 2021 there's no way to know what the value will be for C++2b).

Library vendors typically gate their "C++2a" features on #if __cplusplus > 201703L, and their "C++2b" features on __cplusplus > 202002L, and so on.

Compiler vendors with a "C++2a" mode simply picked any arbitrary value for __cplusplus that made the library vendors' checks happy:

GCC (8.x thru 10.x) -std=c++2a mode uses __cplusplus == 201709L.
Clang (5.x thru 9.x) -std=c++2a mode uses __cplusplus == 201707L.
Microsoft Visual Studio (19.20 thru 19.28) /std:c++latest mode uses __cplusplus == 201705L if and only if you pass /Zc:__cplusplus! Otherwise it uses 199711L. So watch out for that!

How have transitions historically been handled?

Clang 4.0.1 -std=c++1z set __cplusplus == 201406L. Clang 5.0.0 introduced -std=c++17 and -std=c++2a, made -std=c++1z a synonym for -std=c++17, and bumped the macro (no matter which of 17/1z you used) to the standard value 201703L. Clang 10.0 introduced -std=c++20, made -std=c++2a a synonym for -std=c++20, and bumped the macro to the standard value 202002L. As of Feb 2021, Clang has no formal "C++2b" mode.

GCC 5.1 introduced -std=c++1z and -std=c++17 as synonyms out of the gate, setting __cplusplus == 201500L. GCC 7.1 bumped the value (no matter which spelling you used) to the standard value of 201703L. GCC 8.1 introduced -std=c++2a with __cplusplus == 201709L. GCC 10.1 introduced -std=c++20 as a synonym for -std=c++2a (but left the macro at 201709L). As of Feb 2021, GCC trunk has introduced -std=c++2b with __cplusplus == 202100L.

Oddly, according to Godbolt Compiler Explorer, MSVC bumped the macro for -std:c++latest mode from 201704L to 201705L sometime between MSVC 19.16 and 19.20. As of Feb 2021, as far as I know, MSVC has no formal "C++20" mode.

Q: FIND with FINDFORMAT not detecting lines A:

Searching for format is tricky, especially for borders.

Even if you issue an Application.FindFormat.Clear, you have to reset all border linestyles explicitly, else Find will not find anything.

You have another problem with your code: You hardcode the borders 4, 5, 8. However, unless something changed between Excel 2013 and 365 (which I doubt), these values are not correct. According to the documentation, it should be 8 (xlEdgeTop) and 9 (xlEdgeBottom). But don't use numbers, always use the defined constants.

Dealing with xlInsideHorizontal is useless, this is never set for a single cell. It is valid only for ranges that contain more than one row. If you look for cells that are underlined, just search for xlEdgeBottom. The cell below will automatically have set xlEdgeTop, so you could check that without issuing Find.

Independent of the find format: If you want to search for cells that have any content, use What:="*". If you want to search for all cells that are underlined, even if they are empty, use What:=""

A basic piece of code that finds cells that have the botton border set to a black this line looks like this:

' Clear all borders 
With Application.FindFormat
    .Clear
    .Borders.LineStyle = xlNone
End With
' Set bottom borders
With Application.FindFormat.Borders(xlEdgeBottom)
   .LineStyle = xlContinuous
   .ColorIndex = xlAutomatic
   .TintAndShade = 0
   .Weight = xlThin
End With

Dim foundCell As Range
Set foundCell = ws.Columns("A").Find(What:="", LookIn:=xlFormulas, SearchFormat:=True)

A hint for the fruitless discussion with Sergey in the comments: You could simply put a statement Debug.Print diag in your code and C&P the result from the immediate window into your question.

Q: How does wget on macOS handle certificates? A:

I've just encountered this issue five years later with macos brew wget (with brew openssl not working; with curl (although macports) working). I found this post very helpful. Thank you!

Thanks to the tips in this post, I was able to wget and my openssl s_client to work. More recent developments show brew openssl@3 now having a brew dependency on ca-certificates. Maybe other wrinkles have been ironed out as the other methods mentioned by OP worked for me too (saving my Keychain system certs to a pem, using my curl's (although it's macports) cert and passing it into openssl/wget).

In case anyone finds it helpful five years later, the most straightforward fix for me in 2026 was to use brew ca-certificates cert:

$ brew info wget
==> wget ✔: stable 1.25.0, HEAD
...
==> Dependencies
Build (1): pkgconf ✔
Required (5): libidn2 ✔, libpsl ✔, openssl@3 ✔, gettext ✔, libunistring ✔

$ wget "https://httpbin.org/get?x=1"
...
ERROR: cannot verify httpbin.org's certificate, issued by ‘CN=Amazon RSA 2048 M01,O=Amazon,C=US’:
  Unable to locally verify the issuer's authority.
To connect to httpbin.org insecurely, use `--no-check-certificate'.

$ brew info openssl
==> openssl@3 ✔: stable 3.6.3
...
==> Dependencies
Required (1): ca-certificates ✔
...

$ brew ls ca-certificates --verbose
...
/usr/local/Cellar/ca-certificates/2026-08-13/share/ca-certificates/cacert.pem

$ openssl s_client -verifyCAfile /usr/local/Cellar/ca-certificates/2026-08-13/share/ca-certificates/cacert.pem httpbin.org:443 // works
$ wget --ca-certificate /usr/local/Cellar/ca-certificates/2026-08-13/share/ca-certificates/cacert.pem "https://httpbin.org/get?x=1" // works

Q: Can users pretend they have a different location with navigator.geolocation or is it save? A:

Anything done in client-side JavaScript can be overridden by the user, you can't trust it for any security-related purpose.

Some IP geolocation services can identify VPN addresses -- I think MaxMind uses a country code like A1. Services that need to restrict use to particular countries may simply block these since they can't be sure what the actual location is.

If you're willing to trust the user you could fall back to the JavaScript location in this case. If a user is using a VPN to bypass geographic restrictions they could override the JS as well, but it's not as easy. You have to decide how important this check is for you.

Q: How to change Column Collation without losing or changing data? A:

Please do SELECT HEX(col), col FROM ... to see what is stored for "école". Latin1 would look like E9636F6C65. Hebrew, if I am not mistaken, has not include 'é'. See http://collation-charts.org/mysql60/mysql604.hebrew_general_ci.html for what is probably the complete set of characters supported.

Assuming that is correct, do no try to convert to CHARACTER SET hebrew; you will lose information, such as 'é' being turned into '?'.

If you need to store both Hebrew characters and French accented characters (etc), use utf8.

Q: Qt serial port: write and read data A:

If serial.isOpen() && serial.isWritable() is true in while loop, but you can't access it could come from you preferences on your computer.

On OSX: System preferences -> network -> select serial -> advanced -> PPP:
able: Ask to stay connected every 10 minutes,
disable: disconnect at close of session,
disable: disconnect when changing of user
